rows: Hail up to the size of pennies was reported in Lamesa.
HAM radio operator relayed a report from a truck driver on U.S. Highway 87 southeast of Lamesa of quarter size hail covering the road for a mile.
Marble to quarter size hail fell along Farm to Market Road 2051, six miles north of Patricia.
Marble to golfball size hail fell west-northwest of Patricia.
Marble to quarter size hail fell six miles north of Patricia.
Hail up to quarter size fell continuously in Lamesa for half an hour.
Penny sized hail fell northeast of Lamesa.
The Dawson County emergency manager reported 60 mph winds in Lamesa. No damage was reported.
Power lines and a one and a half foot diameter tree were downed by thunderstorm winds in the Forest Park area of Lamesa.
The Texas Tech Universty Mesonet site in Lamesa recorded a 68 mph wind gust. Power lines and at least one tree were downed by these winds.
Strong winds blew a horse trailer into the street.
High winds uprooted trees in Lamesa.
Powerlines were downed due to high winds.
Golf ball sized hail fell along Highway 337 just north of the Dawson and Martin county line.

Members of the Texas Tech Atmospheric Science Group and Greg Morgan from CBS 7 in Odessa witnessed the second tornado, which developed at 3:56 pm CDT, approximately 1.5 miles southwest of Sparenberg over open country, and continued until 4:00 pm. The tornado dissipated approximat…
The Texas Tech Atmospheric Science Group witnessed a well defined, but brief tornado located approximately 4.5 miles northwest of Ackerly. No damage was found.
A brief tornado near Patricia was reported by trained spotters. No damage was reported.
Baseball sized hail fell west-southwest of Lamesa.
Softball sized hail fell in Lamesa.
Baseball sized hail fell in Lamesa.
A brief tornado was reported by a local storm chaser. Estimated loction of the vortex was 2.5 miles west of the intersection of Texas State Highways 349 and 137. No damage was reported.
A second tornado was produced by a strong thunderstorm. The tornado lifted after about 30 seconds. No damage was reported.
Texas DPS reported a brief tornado eight miles west-southwest of Friendship. No damage was reported.
West Texas Mesonet recorded a 62 mph thunderstorm wind gust. No damage was reported.
Power poles southwest of Lamesa were snapped by strong thunderstorm winds.
An estimated wind gust of 60 to 70 mph was reported by a trained spotter along Highway 62/180, 6 miles west of Lamesa, TX. No damage was reported.
There were no damage reports with this gust.

A trained spotter took a photo of a short lived rope tornado near the city of Lamesa, TX. The tornado's track, duration and approximate position were all estimated according to radar data. No damage was reported with this weak tornado.

Significant wind damage was observed within an area 5 miles southeast of Lamesa. Several power poles were knocked over and damaged, trees were uprooted, a large barn and carport were destroyed, and a center pivot irrigation system was flipped over.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and local law enforcement estimated 60 mph wind gusts in Lamesa. No damage was reported.

A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced wind damage in Klondike. A snapped power pole was reported three miles west of Highway 137 on County Road 30. The cost of damage is a rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved over Lamesa and produced a wind gust of 63 mph at the West Texas Mesonet two miles southeast of Lamesa.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 61 mph wind gust two miles southeast of Lamesa.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 58 mph wind gust in Welch.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 72 mph wind gust in Welch.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 62 mph wind gust near Lamesa.

A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 78 mph wind gust two miles southeast of Lamesa.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 58 mph wind gust three miles northeast of Lamesa.
Time was estimated from the radar, and the report was from a tweet on Twitter.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 60 mph wind gust two miles east of Key. There was blowing dust with the winds.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 65 mph wind gust at the mesonet site two miles southeast of Lamesa.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 62 mph wind gust at the Welch mesonet site.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 75 mph wind gust at the Welch mesonet site.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 58 mph wind gust at the mesonet site near Lamesa.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 58 mph wind gust at the mesonet site in Welch.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 62 mph wind gust at the Welch mesonet site.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 72 mph wind gust at the Welch mesonet site.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 78 mph wind gust at the ASOS site near Lamesa.
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced a 73 mph wind gust near Lamesa.

A thunderstorm produced a tornado about two miles east of Arvana. There were multiple reports of a funnel cloud with rotating dust underneath it for three to five minutes. The tornado remained over open fields with no damage reported. The tornado was rated as an EF-0.

A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced wind damage around 12 miles west southwest of Lamesa. There were five snapped power poles at County Road 21 and County Road BB. The time was estimated by radar. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced wind damage near Ackerly. There were 13 snapped power poles one mile north of Ackerly on Highway 87. The time was estimated by radar. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced wind damage in and near Lamesa. Significant wind damage was discovered on the north and northeast sides of Lamesa, Texas. The damage swath included multiple uprooted trees, downed or leaning power poles, metal roofs/carports …
A thunderstorm moved across Dawson County and produced an 88 mph wind gust at the Lamesa mesonet site.

A video shared to broadcast media showed a brief tornado over an open field west of Lamesa. The tornado did not cause any damage and is rated EF-Unknown. The path is estimated from this report and radar data.
A 71 mph wind gust was recorded at the West Texas Mesonet site in Lamesa, in addition to numerous gusts greater than 65 mph.

Lamesa FD/PD reported downed power lines and utility lines. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar and measurements from a nearby Mesonet station. The wind speed was estimated by the extent of the damage reported and nearby Mesonet observations, and the cost of the damage i…
The West Texas Mesonet station 96 Welch measured a number of gusts between 60-80 mph, with the maximum gust reaching 77 mph.

A transformer block was knocked off a power pole towards the south. An empty semi-trailer was also flipped on its side at this location. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The maximum gust and cost of damages is also estimated.
A stop sign was broken away from its base. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar, as is the maximum wind gust.

The doors to a building were blown inward and through the building. Irrigation pivots were found lying towards the southeast. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damages and the maximum wind gust are also estimated.

A fully loaded shipping container was rolled approximately 100 yards towards the southeast. Drone footage showed no clear indication of a tornado path. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damages and the maximum wind gust are also estimated.

A dusty tornado was reported west of Highway 137, northwest of Lamesa. Damage was surveyed at a home, with the awning and trees being damaged. This tornado had an estimated wind speed of 100 MPH and was rated EF-1. Open fields along the estimated tornado path limited the details …
A public report was received via MPING of hen egg-size hail 4 miles southwest of Punkin Center.

Metal roof panels from a small building were found lying to the south and southeast of the building. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damages and the maximum wind gust are also estimated.

Three broken power poles were found lying to the south. These poles were broken near the base or towards the middle. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damages and the maximum wind gust are also estimated.

A metal irrigation spool was thrown 20 yards towards the south-southeast. The spool weighs approximately 200 lbs. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damages and the maximum wind gust are also estimated.
The West Texas Mesonet station 18 Lamesa 2SE measured numerous gusts between 60-80 mph, including a 77 mph gust.

There were reports of damage to signs, power poles, and trees in the town of Lamesa from the public. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damages and the maximum wind gust are also estimated.

The West Texas Mesonet station 96 WELCH Dawson County recorded a couple of severe wind gusts over this 10 minute span of time. The strongest gust was 67 mph.
The AWOS station KLUV Lamesa recorded a 60 mph wind gust. The total time of occurrence is partially approximated.
The West Texas Mesonet station 18 Lamesa 2SE recorded a 60 mph wind gust.
The West Texas Mesonet station 96 WELCH Dawson County measured a 65 mph wind gust, along with several other severe gusts associated with a strong outflow boundary.
A maximum wind gust of 65 MPH was recorded at the West Texas Mesonet station, 18 Lamesa 2SE.
The West Texas Mesonet Station 18 Lamesa 2SE measured a 58 mph wind gust associated with strong thunderstorm outflow.
